notes: §1985:IX.4.2.4 GR2: "Indexed files are classified as belonging to the category of non-sequential single/multi-reel/unit", CLOSE is A (close file: "Closing operations specified by the implementor are executed") and CLOSE WITH LOCK is A, B ("The file is locked and cannot be opened again during this execution of this run unit."). IndexedConnector.Category is NonSequential, and FileRegistry.CloseCell runs that category's close-file cell for every open mode and access mode (flush, dispose, lock release; a host file carries no label records, so no label processing exists to run); BindClose keeps the indexed format to CLOSE and CLOSE WITH LOCK by refusing REEL, UNIT and NO REWIND on a non-sequential file (COBOL1693). The 1985 arm is VisitCloseOption, which accepts WITH LOCK below 2023 (COBOL0902 at 2023); FileClose emits CloseWithLock, which closes and, when the close succeeded, adds the connector to a set that lasts until the run unit ends, and SharedOpenAttempt answers every later OPEN of it with I-O status 38 (§1985:IX.1.3.4). Probed at 85: after CLOSE WITH LOCK, OPEN INPUT, I-O and OUTPUT each give 38; a CLOSE WITH LOCK of a file that is not open gives 42 and locks nothing; a plain CLOSE in mid-file gives 00 and the file reopens at its first record. The lock is the file connector's (another file-name assigned to the same physical file still opens), the reading §2002:9.1.12.5 later prints ("a file connector previously closed with lock"). The witness reopens after a plain CLOSE, then closes WITH LOCK and gets 38 in its USE procedure on the next OPEN.

next.reason: 1985: "CLOSE WITH LOCK | A,B ... B. File Lock The file is locked and cannot be opened again during this execution of this run unit."; 2023: "Table 14 has no WITH LOCK row; non-sequential: CLOSE | c ... c) Close file Closing operations specified by the implementor are executed.". 2023 keeps the non-sequential category and CLOSE as an implementor close. It drops CLOSE WITH LOCK (file lock B) and the label-record processing and its undefined cases.
